errors: "A Job has no liveness probe" — Job pods can have liveness probes; the proposed configuration is unverified.
"a 5-minute index build finishes successfully" — removing the Deployment's probe does not guarantee migration success or establish the Job's timeout.
R01.note: Explains the outage sequence and acknowledges the earlier labels, but substitutes illustrative pseudocode for source evidence and guarantees unverified Job behavior.

errors: "39 of 41 took under 5 seconds" — the facts establish only that most did; the remaining 39 are not all established as under five seconds.
"a 250s build just finishes" — the Job's probes, timeout, and migration success are unverified.
"the running pods keep serving while it works" — compatibility with the changed schema and migration effects on serving are unverified.
"If it's a small column add, it will take about 5 seconds, and nothing breaks" — neither duration nor safety of this migration is established.
"the threshold change would also stop a repeat" — this depends on sufficient probe configuration and successful migration completion.
R02.note: Provides a useful alternative and its observable cost, but invents an exact migration distribution and promises safety for an unchecked schema change.

errors: "39 of the last 41 migrations were under 5s" — only most are established as under five seconds.
"with no probes" — the proposed Job configuration has not been verified.

"a 2min+ index build just delays the deploy instead of taking orders down" — exceeding two minutes does not establish exceeding the 180-second liveness window, and continued API availability requires additional checks.
R03.note: Compactly connects lock waiting to restarts, but leaves the incident and configuration poorly introduced and overstates what the Job guarantees.

errors: "Migrations that take under about 3 minutes work fine" — duration alone does not establish successful migration or deployment.
"a database-wide 'one at a time' lock" — the advisory lock serializes these migration runners, not database activity generally.
"the probes ... fail from the first second" — initial probe timing is not provided.
"a 4-minute index build can't get killed at 180s" — the proposed Job's own probes and deadlines are unverified.
"If it's a quick column add, the entrypoint will handle it as before" — this change's behavior is unverified.
R04.note: Explains the compatibility cost and admits uncertainty about the incident's recovery, but includes unsupported timing and success assurances.

errors: "39 of the last 41 were short" — only most being under five seconds and two exceeding two minutes are established.
"The running pods keep serving while the migration runs" — schema compatibility and migration effects on serving are unverified.
"A 4-minute index build becomes a 4-minute deploy instead of an outage" — total deployment duration and uninterrupted serving are not established.
"today, the first new pod migrates while the old pods still serve" — the current rollout configuration and old-pod availability are not provided.
"If it's a quick column add, today's setup would deploy it fine" — the new migration has not been checked.
"2 of the last 41 did" — two exceeded two minutes; only the incident migration is established as exceeding 180 seconds.
"a pre-deploy Job can't" take the API down — a Job migration can still disrupt serving through schema incompatibility or database effects.
R05.note: Marks one configuration assumption as an inference, but its deciding argument misreads the duration evidence and promises that Job migrations cannot cause outages.

errors: "the existing API pods keep serving while the migration runs" — compatibility is subsequently acknowledged, but database effects and continued serving remain unverified.
R06.note: Gives a concise benefit and compatibility requirement, though the outage sequence omits how startup and lock waiting caused probe failures and shows no configuration lines.

R07.note: Best distinguishes the demonstrated restart failure from unverified migration compatibility and Job configuration, while candidly acknowledging that it cannot supply accurate source lines.

errors: "the kubelet on each node reads" the manifest — the kubelet acts on pod specifications supplied through Kubernetes, rather than directly reading this repository manifest.
"the new pods start, find no pending migrations" — this implies retaining entrypoint migration execution, contrary to the proposed move out of the entrypoint.
"with the Job they start at once" — eliminating migration waiting does not eliminate server startup time.
R08.note: Explains the observable startup difference, but cumbersome definitions obscure it and the proposed behavior ambiguously leaves migration checks in new pods.

errors: "That cycle repeated until the index finally completed" — the incident facts do not establish how recovery occurred or that index completion ended the outage.
"39 finished in under 5 seconds" — only most are established as under five seconds.
"both are in exactly the shape that hit you" — the second slow migration is not established as exceeding 180 seconds or causing this failure.
"the migration no longer runs inside a pod that has probes pointed at it" — the Job's probe configuration is unverified.
"delays the rollout by 4 minutes, with the old pods still serving" — Job duration, schema compatibility, and continued serving are unverified.
"The same 39 fast migrations cost a few extra seconds" — neither that count nor Job overhead is established.
"an index build on a large table" — the table's size is not provided.
R09.note: Includes useful checks for rollout gating and Job timeout, but wraps them in repetition and an invented account of outage recovery.

errors: "Nothing can finish a 4m10s migration" — this is an unsupported absolute about recovery and execution behavior.
"resolved only when someone intervened" — no intervention or recovery mechanism is provided.
"two replicas are guaranteed to be sitting idle-unready whenever a migration runs" — lock contention and simultaneous startup are not guaranteed for every migration.
"a Job pod has no readiness/liveness probe" — Job pods can have probes; this Job is not configured yet.
"it runs the migration to completion" — removing the Deployment's probe does not guarantee completion.
"39 of your 41 recent migrations would've been fine either way" — the duration distribution and counterfactual success are not established.
"slow index builds can't take the API down" — schema changes and database effects can still disrupt the API.
R10.note: Invents intervention and repeated failure details, then replaces the earlier label with another label and several unsupported guarantees.

errors: "hit the 180-second timeout again, and fail in a loop" — repeated timed kills beyond the documented restart and renewed waiting are not explicitly established.
"detaches it from the pod lifecycle" — a Kubernetes Job still runs in pods with a lifecycle.
"The migration can take as long as it needs" — Job and pipeline deadlines are unverified.
"Kubernetes will wait for it to finish before rolling the new pods" — the pipeline must explicitly enforce this ordering; Kubernetes does not automatically couple the Job and Deployment.
R11.note: States the benefit briefly, but omits the lock sequence and attributes pipeline coordination and unlimited runtime to Kubernetes.

errors: "39 of the last 41 migrations finished in under 5 seconds" — only most are established as under five seconds.
"That pod has no server, so the 180s liveness limit doesn't apply" — absence of a server does not determine probe or deadline configuration.
"a 4-minute index build simply finishes" — successful completion and Job timeout are unverified.
"the pods would never get stuck in a restart loop" — gating migration failure prevents this particular rollout failure, not every restart loop.
"raise the liveness limit ... to 10 minutes. That would have prevented INC-212" — this may avoid the documented 180-second kills, but preventing the entire incident is not established.
"the Canva and claude.ai Todoist connectors need authorization" — these connectors and their authorization state are absent from the scenario.
R12.note: Gives a clear failure sequence and an actionable alternative, but adds unsupported guarantees and an entirely unrelated connector-authorization paragraph.
